messages:
Sam C.: Heads-up on a customer case — they see 429 midstream during SSE reconnects and token/usage mismatch in billing. Customer: acme-inc. Started when they rotate auth token every ~30s.

Lina (Support): Thanks Sam. Do we have a repro? any request_id or sample logs?

Sam C.: Repro steps from customer included. Pasting trimmed SSE session below (client rotates token on reconnect):

Client: POST /v1/stream?model=gpt-x with Authorization: Bearer <token-A>
Server: 200 OK
SSE: event: token_info
data: {"session_id":"sess-42","token":"A","seq":0}
SSE: event: partial_output
data: ...
SSE: event: error
data: {"code":429, "message":"quota_exceeded_midstream"}

Client then immediately reconnects with new token: Authorization: Bearer <token-B> and includes same session_id in body.
Client: POST /v1/stream (Authorization: Bearer <token-B>)
Server: 200 OK
SSE: event: token_info
data: {"session_id":"sess-42","token":"B","seq":0}
SSE: event: partial_output
data: ...
SSE: event: done
data: {"usage":{"tokens":120}}

Customer sees billing account charged ~240 tokens even though final done says 120. They claim both sessions got counted.

Lina (Support): Interesting — so midstream 429 then reconnect with fresh token -> double-charge. Any middleware/waf in front of them?

Sam C.: No WAF. They do rotate token frequently for security, it's expected. Attaching trimmed server logs they provided (format: ts | req_id | session | auth_sub):
```
1835002468 | req=aa1 | sess-42 | sub=A | bytes_sent=512
1835002470 | req=aa1 | sess-42 | sub=A | error=429
1835002471 | req=bb2 | sess-42 | sub=B | bytes_sent=640
1835002473 | req=bb2 | sess-42 | sub=B | completed
```

Pri (Ops): I can pull our internal request traces if you want. Looks like two distinct requests (aa1 and bb2) with same session_id but different bearer subjects. Is session_id supplied by client? If so, we currently treat each incoming HTTP request as an independent billing unit — might be where double counting happens.

Devon (Eng): Repro on my side with local curl script that swaps token between reconnects. Can reproduce a 429 midstream when token hits per-token rate quota; reconnect creates new request which our billing pipeline attributes to the new auth identity and doesn't correlate to previous aborted request, so both are billed.

Devon (Eng): Quick notes from debug: our SSE serving runtime creates an ephemeral allocation at request start and writes usage to in-memory counters at response close. If connection closes with non-200 end (429), we flush partial usage to the metering pipeline tagged with the current auth_subject. On reconnect, a new allocation is created and tokens emitted again; client resumes and final usage flushed again. We lack an idempotency/session reconciliation step in metering.

Tanvi (Billing): Oof. So the billing system sees two closes: one error flush (partial count) and one final done. We probably should keep partial counts but mark them as resumed when same session_id + resume_token observed. Need a safe migration path.

Lina (Support): Customer asks for short-term workaround. They can disable token rotation until we patch — not ideal. Any other mitigations?

Devon (Eng): Short-term mitigation ideas:
- Recommend client set a longer-lived session token and reuse the Authorization for the lifetime of the streaming session.
- If client must rotate, include a stable client_session_id in the JSON body and a resume=true header; we can attempt to collapse counts using that id.
- Server-side: suppress partial-usage flush on 4xx/5xx temporary errors and keep them as provisional for X seconds to allow reconnects to reconcile. But that might mask real usage in genuine aborted sessions.

Pri (Ops): I can add temporary log correlator to join requests by session_id and emit a banner for billing that we can use to zero-out double counts manually for affected invoices.

eng-runtime-bot: Canary policy triggered: deploy candidate runtime v1.14.3 to canary cluster due to quota accounting fix branch.

Devon (Eng): I've sketched a fix: attach a stream_session_uuid that is canonical and signed by the control plane. When a request starts, runtime will check if an open session matches and only attribute usage to the canonical session; on reconnect with different auth subject but same signed session id, the usage gets merged. This also requires adding resume tokens to SSE protocol and changing metering consumer to dedupe within a short window.

Sam C.: Timeline? Customer needs ETA for workaround and availability of credited usage if billed twice.

Devon (Eng): Prototype landed in branch: stream-session-reconcile. I'll run canary tomorrow (after QA). If canary looks good, we can ship to prod in 48–72h. Requires migration in metering consumer which Tanvi will coordinate.

Tanvi (Billing): I'll prepare a script to reconcile billed events for acme-inc for the last 24h and issue credit for duplicates once Devon's canary confirms dedupe logic.

Lina (Support): For immediate customer-facing reply: ask them to switch to stable token for the immediate session and we'll proactively credit duplicates while we roll out fix. Also ask for request_ids from their repro to speed match.

Sam C.: Sent proposed reply to acme-inc. They replied: "we can pause rotation for now, but need a permanent fix."

Devon (Eng): Post-canary checklist:
1) Metric: stream_reconnects_by_auth_change — add alarm if > threshold.
2) Metering consumer: dedupe window 60s by session_uuid.
3) Add server header X-Stream-Session: <signed-id> in SSE token_info event for visibility.
4) Update docs and SDK examples to recommend keeping Authorization stable per-stream or use Control-Plane-issued session tokens.

Pri (Ops): I'll add temporary dashboards to track double-count events and a quick runbook for Support to request manual credits.

eng-runtime-bot: Canary deploy started for stream-session-reconcile to canary-1 at 1835002525.

deploy-bot: Canary health: OK (latency + errors within baseline) at 1835002538.

Devon (Eng): Canary observed dedupe working for reconnects with same signed session id; ran replay tests. No increased latency.

Tanvi (Billing): I ran reconciliation for acme-inc and queued a credit for 120 tokens (manual), pending confirmation.

Lina (Support): Customer updated: thanks for fast turnaround, they'll keep rotation paused for today and confirm billing credit received.

Sam C.: Filing internal postmortem + linking this thread in the case.

Devon (Eng): PR merged to main, scheduled rollout next maintenance window. Will post the release notes and docs update.

Pri (Ops): Final note — add explicit logging of resume header and include request_id mapping in archived logs to make future audits simpler.

Sam C.: Thanks all :thumbsup:
